Check the product format before you order

Identify a card from the calendar

This English checklist contains Mega Rayquaza ex at 084/103, 138/103 and 141/103. Our 2026-11-16 check of the PokéCottage English checklist found a 113/076 entry in a separate top-price module; the denominator alone does not establish its language.

Use the matching card number and finish when comparing an individual price.

Is Mega Rayquaza ex the same as an older M Rayquaza-EX?

No. The expansion and collector number identify the printing. A search for Delta Reign Rayquaza can also surface older XY cards named M Rayquaza-EX. These catalog records are useful examples of why the number matters:

A 76/108 card and a 98/98 card are different records even when both depict Rayquaza. Keep their price histories separate. Our Mega Rayquaza printing guide explains the comparison and links to these existing entries. Use a Delta Reign listing only when its own set, image and full number agree with your copy.

How do the Legendary Stadium halves work?

A Legendary Stadium combines two Stadium cards to form extended artwork and a gameplay feature. Pokémon’s announcement says that a booster containing a Legendary Stadium includes both required halves. This is about the contents of a qualifying pack, not a promise of a Stadium in every pack. When checking a listing, confirm whether the seller is offering a pair or one half.

Should you buy packs, an Elite Trainer Box or singles?

Choose a product for the experience you want. Packs provide unopened cards. An Elite Trainer Box adds its stated promo and accessories. A single-card listing lets you select the identified printing rather than opening packs to find it. Compare the sale unit, edition and contents before comparing two totals.

Product contents and listed dates come from the official product showcase. Build & Battle’s November 20 wider availability follows earlier prerelease access: the official expansion page lists prerelease events starting October 24. Those dates describe different purchase windows.

The Center edition’s product identifier is 10-10438-112. Its logo-bearing Kyogre is part of the sealed contents. For dated US offers, membership conditions and box-versus-case comparisons, use the Delta Reign ETB guide. A retailer’s asking price and a manufacturer’s MSRP need separate labels; a large case total also needs its box quantity.

Are the launch retailer promos inside the ETB?

The US launch gift was a separate offer for a qualifying Pokémon TCG purchase of $15 or more. It used the “What’s Your Favorite?” stamp: Groudon at GameStop, Giratina at Best Buy, and Kyogre at Hot Topic, Five Below, Barnes & Noble and Macy’s. The offer began November 6 while supplies lasted, with participating-retailer terms. See the US announcement.

That stamp and the Pokémon Center logo identify different promotions. An ETB’s included Kyogre, a Center-logo Kyogre and a retailer gift should be checked separately. Ask for a clear image of the stamp and confirm whether a listed bonus is included with the purchase. A sealed box’s contents do not establish a store’s remaining gift supply.

How do you confirm the card number and check its value?

  1. Read the full collector number, including both parts of a slash number.
  2. Match the expansion, artwork and language.
  3. Match the finish, such as the specific foil treatment, before choosing a price series.
  4. Read the source, currency and observation date attached to that reference.
  5. Compare the same condition and object type: a loose card, an existing graded copy and a sealed box are different purchases.

The Pokémon catalog and card search are entry points for supported records. CardScanFox’s Delta Reign set currently has no public single-card entries, so use the official material to establish the printing first. A missing catalog row is not a zero value. An older Rayquaza amount does not fill that gap.

For an available record, compare the same price series over time. A large percentage rise can start from a low amount, and a raw reference does not value a graded slab. The raw-versus-graded guide explains that distinction. Record the printing and source with your comparison so you can check like-for-like amounts later.

Where can you check Delta Reign pull rates?

For German-language opening estimates, read our Delta-Herrschaft pull-rate guide. It separates a rarity-tier result from the chance of a particular card and keeps reported samples attributed. Those estimates answer a different question from a checklist or a product’s pack count. A desired single and a box-opening experience are separate buying goals.

What comes in a Delta Reign ETB?

A Delta Reign ETB comes in two versions: the regular box has 9 booster packs and one full-art foil Kyogre promo; the Pokémon Center box has 11 packs and two Kyogre promos, including one with the Center logo. Choose the edition, then compare the purchase quantity and delivered cost.

Included promos and retailer gifts are different offers. Contents follow the official product showcase and Pokémon Center listing, checked 16 November 2026.

Pokémon’s showcase supplies the core standard-box contents. GameStop additionally itemizes six damage-counter dice, six dividers and a TCG Live code. The Center edition adds two packs and a logo-bearing promo to the listed bundle. Its official product page identifies it as SKU 10-10438-112. That identifier belongs to the Center edition; use the exact title and contents when comparing another store’s regular box. Read the Pokémon Center contents and GameStop’s regular-box description.

Which contents should I use when product listings disagree?

For the Delta Reign ETB, use the manufacturer’s description for the exact edition. In our November 16 page check, Pokémon’s standard-box showcase listed 40 Energy cards and a plastic coin. The TCGplayer standard-box description listed 45 Energy cards and two plastic condition markers. These are different descriptions, so we keep the manufacturer’s standard-box specification in the contents table.

For the Center edition, Pokémon Center’s SKU 10-10438-112 separately lists 40 Energy cards, one plastic coin and six dividers. Apply those itemized counts to that Center product. A seller’s generic accessory paragraph should not select a different edition for your comparison.

Which Delta Reign ETB promo or stamp do you want?

There are three different promotion types to recognize. The regular ETB includes its Kyogre card. The Center box includes a regular Kyogre promo plus a Kyogre promo carrying the Pokémon Center logo. A seller describing a “stamped promo” should show which stamp is on the card.

The launch also had a separate US retailer gift offer for eligible Pokémon TCG purchases of $15 or more. Those cards carried a “What’s Your Favorite?” stamp. The official announcement named Groudon at GameStop, Giratina at Best Buy, and Kyogre at several other participating retailers. These gifts were available from November 6 while supplies lasted. A retailer gift is separate from the contents sealed inside an ETB. Check the official US promotion details before planning a purchase around a bonus card.

Delta Reign ETB price, MSRP and availability

US offers checked November 16, 2026: Pokémon Center displayed $59.99 but marked its box UNAVAILABLE, with a purchase limit of two. A TCGplayer regular-box listing showed a featured $84.98 offer with shipping included. Compare the purchase quantity and seller conditions alongside the amount.

Can I buy one ETB at the $80 headline price?

On the captured November 16 Delta Reign ETB listing, the $80 headline offer required at least three boxes. Its item subtotal therefore starts at $240: 3 × $80, before shipping and tax. If you want exactly one ETB, that offer fails the seller’s quantity condition before you compare delivery costs. The separate $84.98 one-box offer showed shipping included on the saved page.

Exactly one ETB No; the seller requires at least three No valid one-box checkout amount from that offer
At least three ETBs The minimum quantity is met Three boxes have a $240 item subtotal; verify shipping and tax at checkout

The row displayed a shipping figure, but shipping for an actual three-box cart was not observed. Enter the delivery amount for your chosen quantity when comparing totals.

Keep the price labels with the numbers. The $59.99 is the Center official-store price; the other rows are seller or retailer offers. These sources do not establish a separate official standard ETB MSRP. Pack-count division compares bundle costs, not the value of cards you will pull.

How should you compare a Delta Reign ETB case?

A single ETB and an ETB case are different sale units. The TCGplayer English case listing describes 10 Elite Trainer Boxes. On November 16, it showed one unopened offer at $711.96 plus $5 shipping. That is a seller’s asking price. The same page showed $793.07 Market Price, $716.95 Most Recent Sale and $825 Listed Median; those are different price measures, not interchangeable checkout offers.

For that advertised offer and its stated quantity:

($711.96 + $5 shipping) ÷ 10 ETBs = about $71.70 per ETB before tax.

Can I buy one Delta Reign ETB with a $100 budget?

Among the three quotes recorded on November 16, 2026 below, the $84.98 single-box offer is the only one whose known order amount is below $100. It leaves $15.02 for tax or other checkout charges. The three-box minimum starts at a $240 goods subtotal, and the ten-box case requires $716.96 before tax. Confirm the remaining checkout charges before deciding that the single-box order fits your budget.

Recorded quote Boxes required Known order amount What it means for a $100 budget
Great Buys single-box offer 1 $84.98, with listed shipping included, before tax $15.02 remains for tax or other charges
San Diego Dawg minimum order 3 $240 goods subtotal; whole-order shipping and tax unconfirmed Already over budget
Ten-box case offer 10 $716.96 with the listed $5 shipping, before tax Already over budget

The single-box headroom is $100 − $84.98 = $15.02 before unknown charges. The minimum-order goods subtotal is 3 × $80 = $240. These are calculations from the dated offers, not a current lowest-price ranking.

Use this order of checks: required edition → minimum boxes → whole-order cost → budget → cost per box or included pack. A case can have a lower unit cost while requiring much more cash. The price-per-pack figure divides a complete ETB bundle, including its promos and accessories; it does not predict the cards you will pull or assign the whole price to loose booster packs.

Compare an ETB quote with your quantity and budget

Enter the edition, desired number of boxes and an optional total budget. Choose a saved quote or use your own confirmed quote. For a case, enter the number of boxes in that seller's sale unit. Add the seller's minimum quantity, shipping for the whole computed order, and checkout tax when you know it.

The calculator rounds the purchase quantity up to the required whole boxes or cases. It then shows the actual boxes ordered, whole-order amount, extra boxes, and cost per box and included pack. Blank shipping or tax stays unknown. An unavailable product or unmet membership condition remains visible beside the arithmetic.

Confirm the seller’s exact case quantity and edition before ordering. title: Pokémon Card Condition Guide: NM, LP, MP & Damage | CardScanFox
description: What do NM, LP and MP mean for Pokémon cards? Learn the raw condition labels, inspect wear and compare the right price context without guessing a PSA grade.
h1: Pokémon Card Condition Guide: NM, LP, MP, HP and Damaged
author: CardScanFox
bodyHtml:
Match the condition as well as the card

Two copies of the same Pokémon printing can need different price comparisons. Identify the set, collector number, language and finish first. Then compare the physical condition of your copy with the condition named by the price source.

TCGplayer uses five raw-card condition labels. The summaries below are a starting point; use its linked standards for a selling decision or a disputed condition.

Label Meaning What to inspect
NM Near Mint Very little wear; small flaws can still be present
LP Lightly Played Limited wear or light scratches; no significant structural issue
MP Moderately Played More visible wear or a combination of moderate imperfections
HP Heavily Played Substantial wear; consult the source’s detailed condition limits
Damaged Damaged Defects that compromise the card’s integrity or meet the source’s damage criteria

What does moderately played mean?

MP describes a raw-card condition, not a numerical slab grade. Under TCGplayer’s guidance, moderate edge wear, scuffing or some bends can fall within this category. Severity matters. A crease caps the condition at MP at best; a bend that compromises structural integrity is Damaged. The detailed guide explains the limits.

Do not decide condition from the front artwork alone. Inspect the back, corners, edges and surface under clear light. Record what you can see rather than assuming that an old card is worn or a freshly opened card is flawless.

Is Near Mint the same as PSA 9 or PSA 10?

There is no direct conversion. TCGplayer’s raw condition labels and PSA’s numerical grades serve different purposes. PSA publishes its own grading standards. A marketplace NM description does not establish a PSA result, and a photo search cannot confirm one.

When comparing an existing slab, use the grading company and number shown on the holder. Read the raw vs graded value guide before comparing a slab with a raw reference.

How condition changes a price comparison

Find the matching record in the Pokémon card database. Read the selected source and condition on the detail page. Where more published reference series are available, select the matching series. A missing LP or MP series is not permission to label the NM amount as that condition’s value.

There is no fixed percentage discount in this guide for moving from NM to LP or MP. The relevant price must match the printing and condition. The observation date matters too.

Keep evidence with your collection research

Note visible defects and take clear front-and-back photos before making a transaction decision. Follow the marketplace’s current standards and the buyer’s stated requirements. Do not flatten, recolor or alter a card to make it fit a condition label.

The CardScanFox app helps identify cards and track holdings. Use AI pregrading for a photo-based condition estimate before submission. Professional authentication and certification remain with the grading company. Confirm the printing and record the condition or existing grade accurately.

title: Delta-Herrschaft Pull Rate: SIR, Mega-Rayquaza & Daten
description: Welche Pull Rate hat Pokémon Delta-Herrschaft? Vergleiche frühe SIR- und Mega-Rayquaza-Schätzungen, Stichprobengrößen und Grenzen für deutsche Booster.
h1: Pokémon Delta-Herrschaft Pull Rate: SIR und Mega-Rayquaza im Vergleich
author: CardScanFox

sources.label: PokéZentrum: Zusammenstellung von etwa 1.850 Packs, 6. November 2026
Pokémon: Dropraten für das digitale TCG Live

bodyHtml:
Wie hoch ist die Pull Rate von Pokémon Delta-Herrschaft?

Stand: 8. November 2026. Es gibt erste veröffentlichte Schätzungen, aber keine von uns verifizierte Ziehquote speziell für deutsche physische Booster. Die hier geprüfte offizielle Pokémon-Ankündigung bestätigt die Erweiterung und den Erscheinungstermin am 6. November. Sie nennt keine Pull-Raten.

Die folgende Tabelle beantwortet die Suche nach „pokemon delta herrschaft pull rate“ mit zugeordneten Quellen. Sie zeigt berichtete Beobachtungen, keine garantierten Inhalte deines nächsten Displays. Delta-Herrschaft heißt auf Englisch Delta Reign. Gleiche Erweiterungsnamen in verschiedenen Sprachen beweisen jedoch keine identische Verteilung.

Erste Schätzungen nach Seltenheit

PokéZentrum berichtet über eine Zusammenstellung aus ungefähr 1.850 geöffneten Packs aus verschiedenen Quellen. Die Veröffentlichung vom 6. November nennt diese gerundeten Werte:

Seltenheitsstufe Von PokéZentrum berichtete Schätzung Bedeutung
Double Rare / Pokémon-ex etwa 1 in 5 Packs Eine Karte dieser Stufe, nicht automatisch deine Wunschkarte
Illustration Rare (IR) etwa 1 in 9 Packs Eine IR aus der jeweiligen Auswahl
Ultra Rare (UR) etwa 1 in 12 Packs Eine UR, nicht eine bestimmte Illustration
Special Illustration Rare (SIR) etwa 1 in 80 Packs Eine SIR; die konkrete Karte ist eine zusätzliche Frage
Mega Hyper Rare (MHR) etwa 1 in 925 Packs Die dort berichtete Schätzung für die goldene Mega-Rayquaza-ex-Karte

Die Zusammenstellung bei PokéZentrum lesen. Wir haben die zugrunde liegenden Öffnungsprotokolle nicht unabhängig geprüft. Die geprüfte Darstellung trennt die Stichprobe nicht eindeutig nach Sprache und Produkt. Deshalb bezeichnen wir diese Zahlen nicht als gemessene deutsche Boosterquoten.

Warum nennt eine andere Quelle andere Zahlen?

TCGtalk beschreibt eine frühere, englischsprachige Vorab-Stichprobe mit 252 Packs. Dort werden vier SIR-Treffer und ein MHR-Treffer gemeldet. Diese kleinen Zähler liefern andere beobachtete Häufigkeiten als die größere Zusammenstellung oben. Ein einzelner Treffer ist besonders empfindlich gegenüber weiteren Öffnungen.

Die englische 252-Pack-Stichprobe ansehen. Auch diese Rohdaten haben wir nicht selbst nachgezählt. Die Seite enthält noch Vorab-Veröffentlichungsformulierungen. Sie dient hier als datierter Vergleich, nicht als aktuelle offizielle Aussage zu deutschen Produkten.

Wir mitteln diese Quellen nicht: Öffnungen könnten sich überschneiden, und Produkt, Sprache sowie Erhebungsmethode sind nicht ausreichend aufeinander abgestimmt. Eine größere Zahl allein ersetzt diese Angaben nicht.

Wie selten ist eine bestimmte Mega-Rayquaza-ex-Karte?

Trenne drei Fragen: Ziehst du irgendeine SIR, eine bestimmte SIR mit Mega-Rayquaza-ex oder eine Karte der MHR-Stufe? Eine Quote für die gesamte SIR-Stufe ist keine Quote für jede einzelne Karte darin.

Ohne Daten zur Verteilung der einzelnen Karten lässt sich die Stufenquote nicht einfach gleichmäßig durch die Anzahl der Karten teilen. Notiere die vollständige Kartennummer, Sprache und Seltenheitsstufe deiner Wunschkarte. Der englische Delta-Reign-Guide erklärt den Unterschied zwischen Erweiterung, Chase Card und konkreter Druckversion.

Ist ein Treffer pro Display garantiert?

Aus einer beobachteten Angabe „1 in 80 Packs“ folgt keine Zusage, dass nach genau 80 Packs ein Treffer kommt. Eine Stichprobe beschreibt gezählte Öffnungen. Sie legt den Inhalt deines nächsten Produkts nicht fest.

Vergleiche zudem Treffer pro Pack mit Treffern pro Pack. Ein Display, eine Trainer-Box und ein einzelner Booster sind unterschiedliche Beobachtungseinheiten. Für eine belastbare Auswertung sollten Quelle, Datum, Sprache, Produkt, geöffnete Packzahl und Trefferzahl angegeben sein.

Gelten die offiziellen TCG-Live-Dropraten für echte Booster?

Die offizielle Droprate-Seite für Pokémon-Sammelkartenspiel-Live betrifft das digitale Spiel. Verwende sie nicht als Nachweis für die Verteilung physischer Booster. Prüfe vor jedem Vergleich, welches Produkt tatsächlich untersucht wurde.

Was tun, nachdem du eine Karte gezogen hast?

Identifiziere zuerst die konkrete Druckversion. In der Pokémon-Kartendatenbank auf Englisch kannst du nach Name, Set und Nummer suchen. Prüfe bei vorhandenen Datensätzen Sprache, Finish, Preisquelle und Beobachtungsdatum. Fehlende Katalogdaten sind kein Nullwert.

Mit CardScanFox kannst du Identifikationskandidaten prüfen und bestätigte Karten deiner Sammlung zuordnen. App und verlinkte Produktseiten sind überwiegend englischsprachig. Eine Pull-Rate sagt weder den Verkaufspreis deiner Karte noch die Wertentwicklung deiner Sammlung voraus.

title: Mickey Mantle Rookie Card Value Guide | CardScanFox
description: Identify the 1951 Bowman Mickey Mantle rookie card, separate it from the 1952 Topps #311, and compare value by condition, grade, and dated market evidence.

author: CardScanFox

sources.label: Heritage Auctions: 1951 Bowman Mickey Mantle #253 PSA Good 2 sale

bodyHtml:
Mickey Mantle card value depends on the year, set, card number, authenticity, condition, and grade. The phrase “Mickey Mantle rookie card” is also used for two different cards, so identification comes before pricing.

Which Mickey Mantle card is the rookie?

The 1951 Bowman #253 is generally recognized as Mickey Mantle's true rookie card. The 1952 Topps #311 is his first Topps card and one of the most important vintage baseball cards, but it is often described as a rookie card in listings and collector conversations.

That distinction matters when comparing sales. A listing title that says “rookie” does not prove that the card is 1951 Bowman. Confirm the set, card number, front design, reverse, and authenticity before using a price guide.

A dated 1951 Bowman #253 sale

Heritage Auctions reported a 1951 Bowman Mickey Mantle #253, PSA Good 2 sale for USD 18,910 on October 25, 2026. Use the set, card number and grade together when you compare this observation with another copy. A single dated sale does not describe every raw or graded condition.

For an ungraded copy, see how to compare raw and graded card values.

1952 Topps Mickey Mantle value

The 1952 Topps #311 has a wide value range because condition and authenticity change the market completely. The PSA CardFacts page provides published guide and population information. Treat that information as dated reference data, not as a guaranteed sale price for a card in your possession.

The main value factors are:

  • Authenticity. A trimmed, altered, recolored, or counterfeit card does not trade like an original example.
  • Condition. Creases, paper loss, stains, centering, surface wear, and rounded corners can move a card across several value bands.
  • Grade. Compare the same grading company and grade whenever possible.
  • Eye appeal. Two cards with the same numeric grade can attract different offers because centering and surface presentation are not identical.

How to identify the card before pricing it

  1. Read the year and set name from the card or holder.
  2. Confirm the card number, especially #253 for 1951 Bowman and #311 for 1952 Topps.
  3. Inspect the front and back for trimming, recoloring, paper loss, stains, and altered stock.
  4. Record whether the card is raw, authenticated, or graded.
  5. Compare the exact version with dated sales and population data.

Do not average a raw card with graded cards. A raw card needs an honest condition assessment. A card in a holder needs the grade and any qualifier read from the label.

Can CardScanFox grade a raw Mickey Mantle card?

CardScanFox's AI card pregrading tool can assess visible condition from uploaded photos and show a manual centering workflow. A photo assessment is an estimate. It does not authenticate the card or replace a professional grade.

For catalog identification and published price references, use the sports card scanner and confirm the exact card record before comparing values.

author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Choose by the job after the scan

A good trading card scanner identifies your exact printing and lets you correct the match before you check a price, save a holding, or list a copy. To choose a Pokémon scanner, use cards with known collector numbers and include two cards with the same name but different artwork or finish. A scan that finds the right character and the wrong printing is a miss for price lookup.

Your task What to try What to check

Scan a stack Try the same small stack in each app Can you correct each candidate before saving and combine duplicates correctly?
Track value after a scan Save one known printing in each app Does the holding keep condition or grade, quantity, source and date?
Sell a card Check a tool’s listing workflow and the marketplace’s sold records Does it show comparable sales and keep listings separate from realized prices?

Run a small comparison

Use the same cards and lighting in each tool. Mark a result as correct only if the set, number, language and variant match. Record candidates you had to correct and cases where the app could not find a match. When free access matters, check whether the limit applies to successful scans, saved cards, price history or batch tools. Check the current plan before paying.

For example, test English Charizard ex 006/165 and 199/165 from Scarlet & Violet—151. Both cards share a name. They should lead to different records. Add a card from a second game if you collect more than one.

Can a scanner also check prices?

Some scanners link to a price reference after you select a catalog match. Use the price for the correct printing and condition or grade, and read its source and date.

title: How to Identify a Trading Card From a Photo | CardScanFox
description: Take a clear photo, verify the exact printing and use a manual search if the match is unclear.
h1: How to identify a trading card from a photo
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Use a clear photo and confirm the printing

Photograph one card from directly above, with the entire front in the frame and the collector number in focus. Use even light and angle the light if foil or a sleeve causes glare. A photo identifier uses the image to find candidates. Match the collector number, set, language, artwork and finish before choosing one.

Check the result in this order

  1. Read the card name and the full number printed on the card.
  2. Compare the set code or symbol and the language.
  3. Check artwork and finish, including any stamp or parallel designation.
  4. Open the matching record. If none matches, search by name and full number, or check the publisher’s database.

For example, a photo of Charizard ex 199/165 may produce other Charizard ex candidates. The full number and artwork distinguish the 151 printing from 006/165 and 183/165.

Choose a photo or a manual search

Use the CardScanFox browser identifier when you have one clear front image. Use the card catalog or publisher checklist if the image is unclear or your language or finish is missing. A manual lookup also works when you can read the number without taking a photo.

Frequently asked questions

What if the first result is wrong?

Check other candidates and compare the printed number. Try a new photo in even light or search the number and set together. Leave the match unresolved if the exact printing is missing.

Can the result tell me whether the card is genuine?

A matching image identifies a possible catalog record. Physical authentication requires separate evidence. See the Pokémon card authenticity guide.

h1: How to identify Pokémon card versions
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Match set, number, language and finish

To identify a Pokémon card version, read its set code or symbol and full collector number. Confirm the printed language and artwork. Then check whether your copy has a different foil pattern, stamp or other finish. Keep all of these details when looking up a price.

Read the small print first

What you see What to record
Set code or an older expansion symbol Use the corresponding release or checklist.
Full number such as 199/165 Save both parts, including leading zeros when printed.
Language and artwork Compare to a checklist or catalog record for that release.
Foil, reverse foil or stamp Match the physical finish and any release mark before choosing a price.

Scarlet & Violet—151 includes Charizard ex 006/165, 183/165 and 199/165 in its English checklist. The shared name does not make the copies interchangeable. In other sets, two finishes can share a collector number. In that case, inspect the foil areas or stamp under light and verify the finish through a catalog or checklist.

Choose the lookup that fits

Use Pokémon’s official checklist to confirm a release and its numbered cards. Use the Pokémon card scanner to find candidates from a photo, then check its answer against the card in your hand. The 151 Charizard guide shows how to compare the three printings without borrowing one version’s price.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Pokédex number the card number?

Use the collector number printed for that set. A Pokédex number identifies a species and can appear on multiple cards.

How do I know whether my card is reverse holo?

Tilt the card under even light and locate the foil. Compare that pattern with the exact set and printing. The treatment can vary by release.

title: How to Check for Fake Pokémon Cards | CardScanFox
description: Compare a suspected copy with the exact Pokémon printing, screen for mismatches, and know when to ask a specialist.
h1: How to check for fake Pokémon cards
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Compare the physical card with a trusted reference

To screen a Pokémon card you suspect is fake, identify its set, full number, language and finish. Compare the front and back, lettering and foil placement with a known genuine copy or official reference for the same printing. Photograph anything that looks inconsistent. A checklist records what was issued and can help you spot a mismatch.

Check multiple details

What to check Example of a reason to look closer
Printing and artwork The collector number belongs to a different card on the official checklist.
Text and layout The card’s spelling or layout differs from the same language and release.
Foil and surface The foil appears in a different area from a matching genuine copy.
Provenance The seller cannot explain the source or provide clear, actual photos.

Pokémon Support suggests checking translucency as one signal and speaking with a specialist card shop when needed. Use low-risk visual checks and avoid damaging the card. Genuine variants can look different, so compare against the same printing.

What AI can check

An AI photo match can suggest what card a copy resembles. It can help you find the record to compare, even when the copy still needs a physical inspection. CardScanFox’s identifier provides possible catalog matches. Its separate photo pregrading tool estimates visible condition from front and back photos. Use a specialist or a professional authentication service when a purchase depends on authenticity.

Frequently asked questions

Can AI reliably detect fake trading cards?

A photo can show some inconsistencies. It cannot establish materials or provenance from an image alone. If the card has value or several details look wrong, ask an experienced specialist to inspect it.

What if a scan finds a valid official card?

Compare the physical copy to that exact edition. A counterfeit can reproduce an existing card’s image and number.

title: Is PSA Grading Worth It? Costs and Outcomes | CardScanFox
description: Compare the raw value, possible grades and full grading cost before deciding whether to submit a trading card.
h1: Is PSA grading worth it?
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Compare the likely outcomes with the full cost

PSA grading may be worth it if authentication or preservation matters to you, or if the expected sale proceeds after grading exceed the proceeds for the raw card by enough to cover fees and risk. Look at completed sales for the exact printing in several grades, including a lower grade than you expect. Calculate shipping, insurance, grading fees and selling fees before deciding.

Work a simple example

Suppose a card could return $60 net if sold raw. Assume a lower grade would return $75 net and a higher grade $130 net before grading costs. If grading and shipping total $40, those two versions return $35 and $90 after that cost. The outcome changes with the grade. These amounts illustrate the calculation. Use current fees and sales for your own card.

Review visible defects on both sides under even light. Use PSA’s official grading standards for the criteria and its service page for current fees. The CardScanFox pregrading tool can estimate visible condition from two photos. A professional grade requires the grader’s own assessment.

Distinguish your options

Keep the card raw if the expense outweighs the benefit or if you mainly want to store it safely. Consider grading when authenticity, an existing set registry goal or buyer confidence matters to you. If you already own a slab, compare that company’s grade and exact printing in the raw versus graded values guide.

Frequently asked questions

Can AI estimate a Pokémon card’s grade?

A clear front and back can support a rough visible-condition range. Glare, blur and hidden surface defects can limit the estimate. PSA defines its own standards and gives the final grade at submission.

Should I use PSA 10 prices when deciding?

Use several plausible grade outcomes, and include the raw alternative. A PSA 10 sale is relevant only for the same printing and grade.

title: How to Organize a Large Trading Card Collection | CardScanFox
description: Sort thousands of cards by game, set and number, record quantities and locations, and reconcile each box before moving on.
h1: How to organize a large trading card collection
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Sort in stages and record each physical location

To organize thousands of trading cards, sort by game, set and collector number first. Keep raw cards and slabs in separate storage. Record each distinct printing, condition or grade, quantity and location. Start with one box before moving the whole collection into your system.

Give each stack a repeatable route

  1. Label a box or binder and assign the stack to a set or a temporary review section.
  2. Use a checklist to order the cards. Put uncertain languages, foil versions or parallels in the review section.
  3. Scan or enter one manageable group. Confirm each record, then record the count and condition or slab grade.
  4. Match the total from the app to the physical count before starting another group.
  5. Keep wanted cards separate from owned cards. Give any future additions a temporary location until you review them.

For example, use a location such as Box A / 151 / tray 2. Two copies of the same Charizard ex printing can share a quantity if condition and location match. Another printing or a PSA slab needs a separate entry.

Keep the app and the storage in sync

A spreadsheet can record locations and quantities if you prefer to maintain every field yourself. An app can speed up identification and pair confirmed holdings with available values. In CardScanFox, use the bulk scan workflow to review images, then use collection folders and the mobile Portfolio to organize copies. Pokémon’s card database can confirm the set when you need a publisher reference.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need to scan every card?

Use manual entry for known duplicates and checklists for obvious matches. Save photo scans for cards you need help identifying, and record incomplete entries in your review section.

How can I track total collection value?

Use the quantity and reference for each exact holding. Keep missing prices visible so you can see which holdings contribute to the displayed estimate.

What is the fastest way to identify a stack of trading cards?

Sort the stack by game and separate pieces that need extra care, such as foils or promos. Group copies you can already identify and count them. Batch the uncertain cards, keep them in photo order and verify results before putting them back. To compare workflows, time a small group from the first photo to the last verified record. Include the time you spent fixing matches. See the mobile bulk scan workflow.

Take and use a card photo

How can I identify a trading card from a photo?

Use one sharp photo of the entire front with the printed number in view. Set the card flat and move the light if a sleeve casts a reflection over the bottom edge. Open the candidate and compare the set, full number, language, artwork and finish. A second photo of the back is useful for reading sports card details when inspecting the candidate by hand. Open the trading card identifier.

Can I scan cards from my camera roll instead of taking a new photo?

Yes. Open the photo picker in a tool that accepts existing images and select a sharp photo of one card at a time. If your camera roll has a binder page in one image, crop a copy around one card and keep its edges and numbering visible. Check the returned card before saving it. Try a saved photo in the CardScanFox web scanner.

How can I identify a sports card from a photo?

Use the front to check the player, sport, team, brand and artwork. Then read the back for the manufacturer, set or copyright information and the full card number. Look for a second number stamped on the card if it appears to be a numbered parallel. A result with the right player and wrong release year needs a second check in the manufacturer’s checklist. Open the sports card scanner · Topps checklists.

How can I identify a card when the text is hard to read?

Start with clues you can see clearly, such as the artwork, logo, border, team or set symbol. Use the image as a search input, then compare suggested records by another visible clue. You can magnify a separate photo or retake it in softer lighting to read a number obscured by glare. Keep the record marked as unknown when the visible clues fit multiple cards. Use the catalog search.

Can a card scanner tell me the set and card number?

Yes, when the tool finds a catalog entry and displays those fields. Open the result and check every character of the printed number, including a prefix, any leading zeros and the denominator. Compare the set code or set symbol too. Some cards share a name or number across releases. Use the publisher’s search if the candidate has missing set data. Pokémon’s guide to the card database.

Distinguish versions and check a suggested match

How do I identify different versions of Pokémon cards?

Read the full collector number, the set mark and the card language. Then check the artwork, foil and any promo logo or stamp. In the English Scarlet & Violet—151 checklist, Charizard ex appears at 006, 183 and 199. The names alone cannot tell you which card to look up. View the publisher’s English 151 checklist · See a printing comparison.

How do I identify a parallel or holographic trading card?

Tilt the card under soft light and check which part reflects. Compare the pattern, border and background color with the checklist for that release. A sports card may also have a stamped serial number such as 08/99. Record that separately from the card’s checklist number. If the same design appears in several foil styles, compare the finish in good light before saving. Find your release in the Topps checklists.

Can a card scanner distinguish English and Japanese printings?

A scanner can suggest a language-specific record when its catalog contains that printing. Check the text on your card and compare the set code, full card number and finish with the suggested record. Artwork can appear in editions with different numbers or release details. If your Japanese card only returns an English suggestion, look up the exact Japanese printing before saving or pricing it. Search the card catalog.

What details should I check after an AI identifies my card?

Check the series or release, printed card number, language and finish on your own copy. Look for details a front image can miss, such as back text, a promo stamp or serial number. After verifying the identity, inspect the actual copy to record its condition. For an existing graded card, use the grader and grade on its label. See what a verified scan result contains.

How do I confirm that an AI card match is the exact printing?

Use the set and number to find the issuer’s entry. Compare the actual language, illustration and surface finish with that entry. A candidate can show the same illustration and card name from a different release, so check the set label on both the screen and the card. For a foil or signed variant, require a match on that feature as well. Follow the photo identification steps.

What should I do when a card scanner suggests the wrong match?

Open the other candidates and compare their full numbers and sets. If none matches, retake the photo with the printed number in focus. Then search the set and number as text. Keep a note that the card is unresolved if the correct printing is missing. This prevents a wrong match from carrying a different card’s price into your collection. Search by card name, set or number.

title: Trading Card Prices and Values | CardScanFox
description: Find the price for your exact card. Compare condition, grade, currency, dated references and completed sales.
h1: Trading Card Prices and Values
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Identify the copy before you price it

A card name can point to several releases. Use the full collector number, set, language and finish to find the right record. Then select a price for the condition or existing grade of your copy.

How much is my Pokémon card worth?

Estimate your card from recent sales or a dated reference for the exact printing in comparable condition. Read the full number and set mark on the card. Check the language and foil, then assess the copy you hold. If the card is already in a grading holder, compare records with the same grader and grade. Browse the Pokémon catalog.

How much is a Charizard card worth by set and number?

Search the set and card number together. For example, the English Scarlet & Violet—151 checklist includes Charizard ex at 006, 183 and 199. Look up the card you own before comparing transactions. Some Charizard releases can also share a number, so record the full set name as well as the digits. Compare Charizard ex printings from 151 · Official English 151 checklist.

How do I find the value of a card with a missing or uncertain number?

Use the name, artwork, language and set symbol to create a short list. Try checking the card back or a better-lit photo of the bottom edge. Compare at least two independent details with a checklist entry before using its price. If you cannot narrow the card to one printing, keep potential matches in separate notes and leave your estimate open. Try the card identifier · Use the official Pokémon card database.

How do language and card condition affect a card value?

Different language printings can serve different buyers. Use recent sales of the language you own. Match the card’s condition by checking visible wear, including scratches, corners, edges and creases. Compare Near Mint prices to another Near Mint copy. Keep an English foil with edge wear in a different search from a clean Japanese copy with similar art. TCGplayer card condition guide.

How do I compare raw and graded card prices?

Use separate groups. Compare a raw card with the same printing in similar raw condition. For a graded card, match the grading company and grade as printed on the holder. Compare a PSA 9 with PSA 9 sales. A PSA 10 and a raw Near Mint copy have separate market records. Report the groups and dates together if you want to see how their prices differ. Compare raw and graded card values.

Find current prices and read the source

What is the best free trading card price checker?

Start with a tool that offers free lookup for your card type and exposes its source and date. TCGplayer publishes marketplace metrics for covered cards. CardScanFox has a browser search by card name, set and number. If you need a specific transaction, search completed sales and compare the card version, condition and currency. Try one familiar card on two services before choosing which to use regularly. Open the card price checker · TCGplayer price metrics.

How do I check the current value of a trading card?

Gather the most recent completed sales you can verify for the exact card and condition. Check the photos and titles for sets, foil and grade. Exclude lots and listings that describe a different version. Compare the middle sold price and the observed range when you have several close matches. Record the currency and sale dates so the estimate can be checked later. Use eBay Product Research.

What is the difference between a listing price and a sold price for a card?

A listing price is the seller’s asking amount. A sold price records what a buyer paid for a completed transaction. TCGplayer’s Listed Median summarizes asks and its Market Price uses recent transactions on TCGplayer. When checking actual sales, note whether shipping is included and whether you can see the accepted price. Read the price definitions.

How can I price a card when no recent sale is available?

Look for older sales of the exact card and record their dates. If you still need a reference, compare a nearby printing or similar release and explain the differences in language, condition, scarcity or buyer demand. Use a wider estimate or leave the price unknown when those differences are too large. For example, keep a previous sale of the exact foil as evidence and an available nonfoil sale as a separate comparison. Read the price data methodology.

Where can I verify the source and date behind a card price?

Open the individual card record and expand its price details. Check the provider, metric, observation date and currency. Confirm the card state and price series you selected. Then compare the provider’s explanation of that metric with the kind of price you need. CardScanFox explains where to find this context on its card pages. Read the card price data methodology.

How do I compare prices across currencies?

Start with the same printing, condition and price metric. Record each original amount and date. Then convert both prices to one currency using a rate for the comparison date. If a rate is quoted as US dollars per euro, divide a dollar amount by that rate to express it in euros. Record the rate source. Add shipping, taxes and currency conversion fees separately when comparing the cost to buy. ECB euro reference rates.

Use price history and maintain a valuation

Where can I find historical trading card prices?

Open a card page with dated observations for the exact printing, then check its price history. For completed transactions, search the same printing on a marketplace and filter dates, condition and sale format. CardScanFox card pages show available observations in the 30 days ending on the selected series’ latest observation. Use dated sales for transaction history and a provider’s chart for its published trend. Read the trading card price history guide · eBay Product Research.

Can a card app show a price history instead of one estimate?

Yes. Look for a dated chart whose source and price type are identified. Choose one series for the exact card and state so the points stay comparable. Open the earliest and latest dates and check that they refer to the same language, finish and grade or raw condition. Extend the time range with marketplace research if you need earlier transactions. Browse card prices.

How often should I recheck a trading card price?

Recheck shortly before buying, selling or submitting a card for grading. For collection tracking, give high-value cards or cards with recent price changes a shorter review interval than inexpensive bulk inventory. Record the observation date and set your next review by how much a stale price would change your decision. An infrequent sale may still leave the best available evidence months old. Check how price dates work.

What is a reasonable way to value a complete card collection?

List the exact printings, split copies by condition or existing grade and count each copy once. Multiply each dated unit reference by its recorded quantity. Sum priced holdings and report the unpriced count beside the total. For many low-value cards, get separate quotes for comparable lots if you plan to sell them together. Deduct fees and shipping separately when estimating proceeds. Learn how to track collection value.

title: How to Check Trading Card Authenticity | CardScanFox
description: Check suspicious cards against official references and look for inconsistencies before seeking an expert opinion.
h1: How to Check Trading Card Authenticity
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Inspect the physical card

How can I tell if my Pokémon card is fake?

Identify the set, full collector number, language and finish first. Compare both sides with a known genuine copy of the same printing. Look for differences in text, image detail and foil placement. If several details disagree and you cannot explain them, keep the card separate and ask a specialist to inspect it. Pokémon Support’s counterfeit card guidance

What physical checks help identify a counterfeit trading card?

Under even light, compare the card’s size, edges, print sharpness, surface and back design with a known genuine copy of the same issue. Tilt both cards to see where reflections appear. Pokémon Support suggests a bright-light check as one clue for Pokémon cards. Compare both cards under the same conditions, and leave the stock intact. Pokémon Support’s counterfeit card guidance

What signs suggest a Pokémon card may be counterfeit?

An incorrect attack name, a collector number paired with the wrong artwork, or foil in an unexpected area gives you a reason to investigate. For sealed packs, compare the packaging with the official product images and ask how the seller obtained it. Pokémon Support also flags unusually low pack prices. Pokémon Support’s counterfeit card guidance

How should I handle a card with an unusual font or color?

Photograph both sides in neutral light and check the set and language before comparing the print. Screen settings and lighting can change how colors appear. Look for multiple differences that persist across new photos, such as different letter shapes and misplaced symbols. Keep the images and the listing for a specialist if the discrepancy remains.

Confirm the printing from a photo or checklist

Can AI detect fake trading cards?

AI can help you notice visible inconsistencies and find a reference image. A photo rarely shows enough detail to verify paper, ink or prior alterations. CardScanFox returns possible catalog matches. Use a physical inspection when a purchase or sale depends on the card’s authenticity. CardScanFox card identifier · CGC Cards grading process

Can a scan prove that a trading card is authentic?

No. A confident match shows that the image resembles a catalog record. A counterfeit may reproduce its artwork and collector number. Use the scan to decide which genuine printing to compare, then examine the physical copy. CardScanFox card identifier

What should I do when a card looks real but the catalog match is uncertain?

Search the catalog by the full printed number and narrow the results by set. Check the set code, artwork, language, stamp and finish before saving a match or using its price. If the catalog lacks the exact printing, use the publisher’s checklist or leave the ID unresolved. Pokémon Support’s database guide

How can I compare a suspicious card with an official checklist?

Open the publisher’s checklist for the exact release and language. Find the full collector number. Check the matching name and rarity, then use the official database art or a known copy to check the layout and finish. The English Scarlet & Violet—151 checklist lists Charizard ex at 006, 183 and 199. A seller’s photo and number must refer to the same printing before you use it as a comparison. A checklist can confirm a design was issued. A physical inspection assesses the copy. Official Pokémon TCG Scarlet & Violet—151 checklist · Charizard 151 printing examples

Check the listing and decide who can help

Can price data tell me whether a card is fake?

Use price to decide whether the listing needs a closer look. Compare it with completed sales of the same set, number, language, finish and condition. A low price can also reflect wear, a different variant or a seller’s need for a quick sale. Ask for clear photos of the actual copy and check the return terms. eBay Product Research

Who should I contact for a professional authenticity opinion?

A specialist trading card shop can help you inspect a questionable copy in person. For a formal assessment, check whether a professional service such as PSA or CGC Cards accepts the issue and assesses authenticity. For a slab you already own, match the issuer’s certification entry, card details and available images to the holder. PSA says that a valid certification number still leaves risk because a counterfeiter can copy one. PSA trading card grading · PSA certification verification · CGC Cards grading process

title: Trading Card Grading, Costs and Grades | CardScanFox
description: Decide when to grade a card, check raw and slabbed prices, and understand what a photo estimate can show.
h1: Trading Card Grading, Costs and Grades
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Understand what a grade describes

What is the difference between a raw card and a graded card?

A raw card has no current third-party condition grade. Terms such as Near Mint describe the seller’s or collector’s assessment. A numerically graded card has a grade from a specific company and typically comes in that company’s labeled holder. Check the label for the company, grade, card identity and any special designation. Raw versus graded card values · CGC Cards grading process

Which card conditions matter most before grading?

Check centering, corners, edges and the surface on both sides. Use angled light to reveal dents, scratches and print lines, and check the corners and edges for whitening or small chips. Save your photos and compare what you can see with the service’s published standards. A clean border alone gives you little information about a dent or faint crease. PSA grading standards · CGC Cards grading scale

Can AI estimate Pokémon card grades?

AI can estimate a range for visible condition from sharp front and back photos. Even light helps you compare centering, corners and edges. Angled light can expose flaws that the first photos miss. If a sleeve hides an edge or glare covers part of the surface, retake the photos or treat that area as uncertain. CardScanFox photo pregrading · PSA grading standards

Can a photo replace an official grading service?

Use photos to screen cards before sending them in. A grader can examine the physical card for surface flaws, authenticity and alterations with tools a photo cannot provide. A recognized grade and a certification record require the grader’s own process. CGC Cards grading process

Decide whether to submit

What should I check before sending a card for grading?

Verify the full printing and confirm that your grader accepts it. Inspect both sides and photograph the card while you can document its condition. Then check the service tier, maximum insured value, packing instructions, turnaround estimate and return shipping. Avoid trying to remove a mark or press a crease. PSA lists evidence of cleaning and altered stock as reasons it may decline a numeric grade. PSA trading card grading · PSA grading standards

Is PSA grading worth it?

It can be worthwhile if authentication and a holder matter to you, or if a realistic grade leaves enough extra sale proceeds to cover all costs. Compare the amount you could receive for the card raw with completed sales at several plausible grades. If the numbers work only at PSA 10, you are relying on that outcome. PSA grading decision and worked example · PSA trading card grading

How do PSA 10 and PSA 9 prices usually differ?

PSA 10 can sell for more than PSA 9, but there is no fixed multiplier. Compare recent completed sales for the same set, number, language and finish, and keep sales of each grade in their own group. Report the sale count and date range if the card trades rarely. If three comparable PSA 9 sales cluster near $90 and three PSA 10 sales near $150, that sample shows about a $60 difference before costs. Those amounts are illustrative. PSA Auction Prices Realized · eBay Product Research

How do grading fees and shipping affect the decision?

Add the grading fee, shipping in both directions, insurance and any other charges shown at submission. For a group of cards, divide the shared costs across the cards before comparing the options. Deduct selling costs separately from the raw and graded sale scenarios. Use the grader’s price and turnaround estimate for your region and tier. PSA trading card grading

When is grading a low-value card not worthwhile?

For resale, grading usually makes little sense when realistic graded proceeds after costs are below the raw proceeds. If you could receive $12 net selling raw and $30 net selling graded before $25 of submission costs, the graded path would return $5. Grading can still serve a personal collection goal if you are comfortable paying for the service. Raw versus graded card values

Record a slab you already own

How should I record an existing slab grade in a collection app?

Save the exact printing and the company and grade printed on its slab. For example, keep a PSA 9 copy and a Near Mint raw copy as separate holdings. If your app has a field for the certificate number, enter it and compare the issuer’s record and images with the slab. In CardScanFox, choose the grader and grade for the copy you own, then use a price series for the same company, grade and printing if available. CardScanFox graded card tracker · PSA certification verification

title: How to Organize a Trading Card Collection | CardScanFox
description: Record holdings, separate duplicates by printing and condition, and track portfolio value without treating missing prices as zero.
h1: How to Organize a Trading Card Collection
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Build a record that matches the card you own

Use one record for each group of copies that share a printing and condition. Record the location so you can check the physical card again when a price changes or you want to sell it.

What fields should a digital card collection include?

Start with the game or sport, set, full number, language, finish, condition, quantity and location. Add the card name for search and include the release year and manufacturer when they help identify a sports card. For graded copies, keep the grading company, grade and certificate number from the label. If you track values, give purchase cost and market reference their own fields. Add a date, currency and price source to the reference. An entry such as 151, Charizard ex 006/165, English, binder A, page 4 lets you find the physical card and verify the result. Read the collection app selection guide.

What is a good workflow for adding a new card to a collection?

  1. Find the card by photo or search. Compare the set, full collector number, language and finish.
  2. Record the condition you inspected or the existing grade printed on the holder.
  3. Add the quantity and physical location. Record the acquisition date or purchase cost if you track them.
  4. Open the saved holding and compare those fields with the card. Note any missing price and place the physical card in its assigned location.

CardScanFox’s mobile Portfolio tracks cards you own. Use Wishlist for cards you intend to get, and browser Saved for card references. See the collection tracker.

How do I keep raw and graded cards separate in my collection?

Give raw and graded copies separate records. Inspect raw copies using the condition guide for your selling market. For a graded copy, record the label’s grading company, grade and certificate number. An English raw Lightly Played copy and a PSA 9 copy of the same printing should remain separate even if they sit in the same box. For a PSA slab, compare the number and recorded details with PSA’s lookup. TCGplayer condition guide · PSA certificate verification.

How can I find duplicate cards in a collection?

Group entries by game, set, full number, language and finish. Within each group, check condition and whether any copies are graded. Then check physical locations and reconcile the recorded quantity. If the same record was added twice for one copy, correct the count. If you own two identical copies, keep both in the count. Keep a separate entry or certificate detail for individually graded copies. See the folder and binder workflow.

Organize a large or mixed collection

What is the best way to organize thousands of trading cards?

Give each box and binder an ID, then group cards by game, set and number. Process one tray, box or binder page at a time. Count known duplicates as a group and scan the cards you cannot identify by hand. Keep a small review section for uncertain printings. Record the physical location with the entry so you can find a card without scanning the same stack again. Read the large collection workflow.

How do I track cards from multiple games in one collection?

Keep one collection with a game field and filters for each game. Retain set, collector number, language and finish on every record because those details can overlap between games. Try adding a Pokémon card and a Magic card, then filter by game and verify that each entry still shows its correct set and condition. Keep a manual inventory note for any printing your tracking app cannot match. Browse the CardScanFox catalog by game.

Track collection value and prepare cards to sell

How can I track the value of my card collection?

Use one dated price reference for each priced holding. Multiply by the number of copies in that condition or grade. Keep a count of holdings with no price and show it next to the total. Record purchase costs separately if you want to track what you spent. Before selling, check recent comparable sales for your highest-value cards. A collection total gives you an estimate before fees, shipping and discounts. Open the collection tracker.

How can I monitor collection value over time?

Save a dated snapshot with your holdings, quantities, coverage and total estimated value. When the total changes, check whether prices moved on cards you held throughout the period or whether you added or removed cards. Compare the same set of holdings using the same price sources for a view of price changes alone. If a card gains a price for the first time, record that as a coverage change. Read how to compare dated prices.

How should I record cards with missing prices?

Keep their identity, condition, quantity, location and last lookup date. Mark the valuation as unavailable and include those copies in the inventory count. Show how many copies contribute to the estimated total so readers can see what is missing. If you add a manual estimate later, keep its source, date and accepted range next to the amount. See how missing prices are displayed.

How do I prepare a collection list before selling cards?

Check the digital list against the physical cards you plan to sell. Record the exact printings, language, finish, condition and quantity. Group bulk separately from individually priced singles. Photograph both sides of important cards and show any wear or stamps clearly. For slabs, check the cert and include the grader and grade on the listing. Use dated comparable sales to choose a price and estimate fees and shipping separately. eBay seller pricing guide.

title: How to Sell and Ship Trading Cards | CardScanFox
description: Prepare a collection for sale, match exact printings, compare sold prices and pack singles or slabs for shipping.
h1: How to Sell and Ship Trading Cards
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Choose how to sell

Check the printing and condition first. Then compare what you would keep after fees, shipping and the time it takes to list each card. The market examples below use U.S. seller rules. Check eligibility and shipping terms for your location.

Where can I sell trading cards?

Use eBay if you want to choose between a fixed price and an auction. Check TCGplayer for supported trading card game singles that match an existing catalog record. Ask a local card shop for a quote when you want to move a whole collection. For example, compare the cash quote for 100 cards with the proceeds from selling the five most valuable singles and grouping the other 95 together. Include fees and shipping when you compare the options. TCGplayer seller app · eBay sold-price research

How do I prepare a trading card collection for sale?

Sort the collection into raw singles, graded cards, sealed products and bulk lots. Record the set, full number, language, finish, condition and quantity. Check both sides of each valuable single and photograph the copy you plan to sell. If you find three copies of the same card, inspect each one. A crease on one copy can change its listing even when the other two also share its printing. Collection inventory workflow · TCGplayer listing photo policy

List and ship the exact item

How can I avoid using the wrong printing when listing a card?

Match the set, complete collector number, language and finish before publishing. Check the artwork and any edition stamp against the physical copy. A photo scan can give you a candidate, so read the number on the card before using the match. For example, an English Charizard ex from Pokémon 151 with 199/165 needs a different listing from Charizard ex 006/165. Fix the marketplace draft if its suggested details disagree with the card. Pokémon printing guide · eBay Scan to List help

What information should a card listing include?

Give the buyer the game, name, set, full number, language, variant, quantity and condition. Show the front and back of the exact item and describe damage or alterations. If the card is slabbed, include its grading company and grade, with a readable label photo. Put the asking price in the platform's price field. As a check, ask someone to identify the copy and find any flaws from the listing alone. TCGplayer listing photo policy

How do I compare an asking price with recent market evidence?

Compare recent completed sales of the same printing, language, finish and card condition or certified grade. Note the dates and currency, and handle shipping the same way for every sale. For example, if three matching item prices are $32, $35 and $40, the median is $35 before shipping. Treat a $60 asking price as the seller's proposed amount. A single comparable sale is still useful if you record the limited sample. eBay Product Research · Trading card price history

Where can I sell graded Pokémon cards?

Compare an eBay listing with a local shop offer or a consignment service. PSA offers eBay consignment options for eligible vaulted cards. Check the grading company, grade, selling fees and payout terms before you choose. Compare several completed sales of your exact Pokémon printing in the same grading company's holder and grade. If you own a PSA 9, start with other PSA 9 sales from the same set and full card number. Sell with PSA · eBay trading card authentication eligibility

How should I package trading cards for shipping?

Place a raw card in a fitted sleeve and use a holder that the shipping service accepts. Prevent the card from shifting, keep adhesive away from the card and protect the parcel from bending and moisture. For a slab, choose a padded parcel with cushioning around the case and select tracking or insurance according to its value and the sales platform's rules. Give the packed parcel a gentle movement check before sealing. The U.S. eBay standard envelope excludes graded cards, and PSA grading submissions have their own packing instructions. TCGplayer buyer-order shipping guide · eBay standard envelope · PSA shipping guide

Check a purchase or value a collection

What should I check before buying a valuable card online?

Read the seller's feedback, the return terms and the photos of both sides. Compare the listing with sales for the same printing and condition. For a graded card, check the certificate with the grading company and compare the record with the photographed label, card and holder. A matching number verifies the database record. For a suspicious or expensive purchase, check whether the listing qualifies for a platform authentication service or ask a qualified professional to inspect the card. PSA certificate verification · eBay buyer authentication eligibility · Card authenticity checks

How do I separate a sealed product from a single-card value?

Keep separate rows for the unopened product and for each single. Match a sealed item's exact edition, contents and seal condition to other sealed sales. Match a single by its full card number, printing and condition or grade. For a Pokémon 30th Anniversary Ultra-Premium Collection, check which edition of the box you have and look up sealed sales for that edition. Value a specific promo or opened pull using a separate single-card record. Pokémon 30th Anniversary Ultra-Premium Collection guide · Pokémon 30th Celebration card and price guide

How can I make a card inventory for an insurance or estate record?

Keep a dated inventory with identifying details, quantity, condition, any certification number, acquisition records, photos and storage location. Back it up somewhere separate from the collection. For your ten highest-value cards, check that each pair of photos and receipt can be matched to the correct record. Ask the insurer or estate professional which valuation date and documents they require. Record the source of any estimate and keep app reference prices separate from a formal appraisal. NAIC home inventory guidance · Collection inventory workflow

title: How to Read Trading Card Market Trends | CardScanFox
description: Compare trading card interest and prices with a consistent date window, platform and printing.
h1: How to Read Trading Card Market Trends
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Read price and demand signals

Start with the exact card, then choose a source that measures the question you are asking. Search rankings measure interest. Sold listings measure transactions within a marketplace. The CardScanFox weekly gainers list measures changes in matched, published raw-card price series.

What are the current trading card market trends?

As of November 24, 2026, eBay's Collected report gives a dated view of buyer searches. Charizard led Pokémon character searches on eBay.com from January through September 2026, followed by Pikachu and Gengar. The same report shows different leaders by U.S. sports league. These observations describe searches on that platform and in those periods. To check prices, pick a single printing such as English Charizard ex 199/165, then compare completed-sale counts and median prices over equal recent windows. eBay Collected 2026 · eBay Product Research

Which trading card categories are growing in interest?

Compare each category with its own earlier period using the same geography, source and time window. For example, compare U.S. search interest for Pokémon cards and One Piece cards across equal 90-day periods, then check completed sales for each category. Put search terms in one Google Trends comparison so they use the same scale. The eBay January–September 2026 report gives examples of popular Pokémon characters and athletes. A ranking needs a comparable earlier period before you can describe growth. Google Trends data FAQ · eBay Collected 2026

How should I read a trading card price trend?

Follow the same printing, finish, language, raw condition or grading company and grade across all dates. Read the chart's source, currency and price metric. If one month has two matching sales and another has 20, write down both counts alongside their median prices. A sparse month gives less evidence about a typical sale. CardScanFox shows available observations for the selected series in a 30-day window. An empty day has no reported value in that series. Trading card price history · CardScanFox price methodology · TCGplayer price points

What makes a card price change over time?

Prices can move when copies become easier to find, a reprint appears, players need a card for a deck or collectors seek a scarce grade. Before attributing a jump to an event, check how many comparable copies actually sold and whether the card, grade or price series changed. For example, compare the sale dates and counts before and after an announced reprint. If only one matching sale occurred after the announcement, keep the explanation tentative. TCGplayer price volatility and metrics · PriceCharting methodology

How can I research a card without treating it as a guaranteed investment?

Set a budget that works for you even if resale takes time or prices fall. Record your purchase cost, tax, shipping and any appraisal or grading fees. Then estimate net resale from matching sales after seller fees, with a lower-price scenario. In a hypothetical example, a $60 total cost and $50 in resale proceeds after fees would leave a $10 shortfall. Historical prices describe past observations, and your future sale depends on finding a buyer. Trading card price history · eBay sold-price research

title: How to Start Playing Trading Card Games | CardScanFox
description: Choose a game, learn from official starter resources and check format rules before building a deck.
h1: How to Start Playing Trading Card Games
author: CardScanFox Editorial
bodyHtml:
Start with a game you can try

Try a game that has a ready-to-play deck and someone nearby or online to play with. Before buying individual cards, confirm which format your group plays. Use the publisher's current rules for deck size, allowed cards and copy limits.

What trading card games are good for a new player?

Pokémon Battle Academy suits two people learning together with guided decks. Magic Academy offers beginner sessions at participating stores. Disney Lorcana provides short tutorials on turns and resources, and Konami publishes a Yu-Gi-Oh! beginner guide. Pick a theme you enjoy and try a short game with a starter deck. If you need a local opponent, check which of these games a nearby store actually teaches. Pokémon learning resources · Magic Academy · Disney Lorcana tutorials · Yu-Gi-Oh! beginner guide

How do I start building a deck for a trading card game?

Pick a game, a format and one plan for how your deck wins. Use a publisher starter list as a baseline. Check deck size, allowed cards, resource costs and copy limits. For example, Magic Standard starts at 60 cards. One Piece uses a leader, a 50-card main deck and a separate 10-card DON!! deck under its official rules. After a few practice games, note which hands could not support your plan, then change a small number of cards and try again. Magic Standard rules · One Piece Card Game rules

How can I identify which game a card belongs to?

Read the game logo, card frame, set mark, full number and rules text. Use the publisher's gallery or card database to confirm an exact match. For example, for a suspected Pokémon card, search its printed card name and compare the expansion and illustrations in Pokémon's database. A character can appear in a separate game or a non-game product, so use the markings on the physical card to confirm the category. Pokémon database help · Browse games · Card identifier

What is the difference between collecting cards and playing a card game?

A collection tracks what you own and the copies you want, such as a specific printing or a complete set. Play uses cards that fit your deck's plan and the event's rules. Before buying a card for an event, check the format even if an attractive printing fits your collection. For example, keep a display copy in your binder and check which copies your game permits in your deck. Pokémon collecting and play · Magic formats · Collection organization guide

How should I organize cards for deck building?

Separate games first. Within each game, group cards by categories you reach for when building, such as color, resource cost, card type or a particular role. Give decks in use their own boxes and record how many spare copies remain. For example, take your current deck list and see whether you can find a replacement resource card and a support card from the storage labels. Recheck format legality before bringing the deck to an event. Magic formats · Card collection organization

title: How to Store and Protect Trading Cards | CardScanFox
description: Choose protective sleeves and storage for raw and graded cards. Reduce damage from handling, humidity, heat and light.
h1: How to Store and Protect Trading Cards
author: CardScanFox Editorial

sources.label: Canadian Conservation Institute paper objects guidance

bodyHtml:
Protect cards from handling and their surroundings

Keep cards in fitted protective holders in a clean indoor space with stable conditions. Choose holders that fit the size and thickness of the item. Look after the original slab for cards that already have a professional grade.

How should I store trading cards long term?

Use clean, fitted sleeves and a well-supported box or binder. Choose an indoor shelf off the floor, away from pipes, vents and direct sunlight. Keep the cards supported so they cannot lean hard or slide. For example, inspect one box after a humid season. Check the lid and inside surfaces for damp marks, and look for cards that have curled or shifted. Canadian Conservation Institute paper care

What sleeves and binders help protect cards?

Pick sleeves and binder pockets that fit the full card, with room for its thickness. Look for a manufacturer that identifies the material, such as non-PVC polypropylene. A thicker memorabilia card may need a dedicated holder. Slip a low-value card of the same dimensions into a sample pocket first. If the corners catch or the page bows, choose a larger pocket or a holder sized for the thicker card. Ultra PRO binder guidance · Canadian Conservation Institute enclosure guidance

How do humidity and heat affect trading cards?

High humidity can encourage mold. Repeated swings can make paper expand and shrink, which can cause distortion. Heat can speed up paper deterioration, and direct light adds fading risk. Place a hygrometer near your collection and record readings through a wet week. If conditions swing sharply beside a window or exterior wall, move the cards to a more stable indoor shelf. Preservation guidance for paper gives context, and different card coatings and holders can respond differently. Canadian Conservation Institute storage guidance

What is the safest way to store valuable graded cards?

Keep the grading holder intact and use a fitted case or padded cabinet so slabs stay separated and protected against knocks. Store the case in a stable, secure location away from water and sunlight. Keep a separate record of each label and photographs of both sides. For a collection that needs professional storage, check service eligibility, policy coverage and retrieval terms. PSA Vault lists eligible grading companies and publishes its service terms. PSA Vault · PSA Vault terms · Graded card tracking guide

How can I photograph cards without damaging them?

Set a camera above a clean, dry, flat surface and use even, indirect light. Handle a raw card by its edges with clean, dry hands. Keep an existing slab or protective sleeve in place when the label and edges are readable. If the photo catches glare, move the light or camera before handling the card again. Review the front and back images for visible corners and legible set numbers before you put the card away. Canadian Conservation Institute handling guidance · Identify a trading card from a photo
